arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Ali argued that the Second Circuit's requirement for an affirmative finding of innocence is wrong.
Mr. Ali stated that a proceeding ends favorably when the prosecution fails to obtain a conviction.
Mr. Ellis argued that the claim is analogous to a malicious prosecution claim.
Mr. Ellis noted that common law purposes include avoiding inconsistent criminal and civil judgments.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the standard for ending a criminal case in a plaintiff's favor. The dispute centers on whether a civil claim requires proof of innocence or merely the failure to convict.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The standard determines when a civil claim can proceed after criminal charges end. A lower standard allows more suits to move forward. A higher standard blocks suits unless innocence is explicitly found.
